title: Interactive checkpointed admin shell for safe runbook execution
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: on-call engineers run ad-hoc playbooks and long runbooks with multiple mutation steps; current runbook runners either (a) execute as a batch (risking large blast radius) or (b) require manual step-by-step commands with poor auditability. Goal: provide an interactive admin shell that treats runbooks as checkpointed tasks: each checkpoint is a safe point that can be inspected, skipped, retried, or rolled back. The shell should be usable from Console (web) and Admin CLI, include typed inputs for each step, enforce RBAC and 2-step confirmations for destructive actions, persist checkpoints to audit log, and expose safe rollback primitives for a constrained set of actions (feature-flags toggles, infra scale down/up, queue drains). Deliverables: (1) a small runtime that wraps existing runbook task definitions with checkpoint semantics, (2) a web-based interactive console view with step inspector and rollback controls, (3) CLI parity and scripted dry-run mode, (4) telemetry so SREs can measure step-level latency, errors, and rollback counts. Constraints: must reuse existing runbook DSL (no schema migration), fit into current auth scopes (console tokens, SSO), and not increase median runbook latency by more than 15% in non-interactive runs. Security: all rollbacks require audit annotation and SSO identity; KMS-encrypted rollback tokens for cross-region operations. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated beta (non-prod) -> invite SRE + 2 customer-facing oncall teams -> widen to platform oncall -> GA with 90-day incident review.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive shell can load existing runbook by key and show typed inputs for next step
Checkpoint created after each successful step persisted to audit log with actor and timestamp
Rollback API for supported actions exists and requires explicit annotation
CLI and Console show identical step state and allow resume/skip/retry actions
Telemetry emits events for step.start, step.complete, step.rollback with runbook key and duration
implementation_notes: Implement checkpoint store as append-only records in existing ops-events table; avoid new DBs
Wrap current task executor with a minimal state machine: PENDING -> RUNNING -> CHECKPOINTED -> COMPLETED -> ROLLED_BACK
For rollbacks, implement action-specific compensators; start with a whitelist: feature-flag, deployment-tag toggle, redis key reset, queue pause/unpause
UI: reuse runbook-editor UI primitives but add step-inspector panel and confirmation modal with typed input preview
Auth: check token scopes; destructive actions require token with 'admin:runbooks:rollback' and SSO reauth for >P1 ops
risks: Rollback compensators may not be idempotent for all existing tasks; must restrict to safe subset initially
Cross-region rollbacks require careful KMS key design and could delay rollback by seconds to minutes
Operators may over-rely on rollback if compensators are imperfect — mitigated by 'dry-run' default and telemetry alerts
